html:
The Serrano are a Native American people of the San Bernardino Mountains and the edge of the Mojave Desert in southern California. Yuhaviatam means "people of the pines", and the Maarenga'yam lived at the oasis of Twentynine Palms. They speak a Takic language of the Uto-Aztecan family.

They gathered acorns and pine nuts, hunted, and lived in clan villages by springs and streams. The Spanish called them Serrano, "mountain people". Their neighbours were the Tongva to the west, the Cahuilla to the south and the Chemehuevi in the desert.

From the late 1700s Mission San Gabriel took in many Serrano, and disease spread through the mountains. Their descendants live mainly at the San Manuel and Morongo reservations. See also Serrano.
